scores and estimates unchanged; previously:; Pathfinder › Trap: the Pathfinder panel's Trap… and Effect › Pathfinder › Trap… add overprinting traps of the lighter colour where solid colours meet; no entry closed; Artboard Options: Show Video Safe Areas (showVideoSafeAreas) outlines the action-safe and title-safe areas 3.5% and 5% in from each edge (EBU R 95) on the canvas only, and Video Ruler Pixel Aspect Ratio (videoRulerPixelAspectRatio, 0.1–10, default 1) sets how wide a video pixel is, per artboard, in one undo step and in the native format; estimates unchanged; Fix #3705: in Draw Inside, art drawn or pasted inside the isolated object takes isolation mode into its clip group, so it can be clicked and isn't dimmed; undo or redo that removes the isolated object ends isolation mode; Feature submission evidence

Feature evidence last updated: 2026-10-22.

The shared assessment status line and revision history are current upstream; this dated section records the submission's feature evidence and revisions without rescoring upstream or claiming a new combined build or runtime measurement.

  • Current-main conflict reconciliation retains upstream and feature behavior; scores and estimates unchanged

  • Superseded 2026-10-20 behavior, retained as history: Artboard Options shares existing presets and orientation controls and can fit artwork without moving it; artwork fitting uses the original target artboard and revision-scoped bounds caches

  • Artboard Options puts Fit to Artwork Bounds and Fit to Selected Art in the Preset menu. Artwork bounds cover all drawn document art, including other artboards and off-board art; selection bounds may span artboards. Fit changes only the active artboard and keeps artwork stationary, including position-only fitting with Move Artwork enabled. Existing Background Color and presets remain available; scores and estimates unchanged.

Artboard Options forwards the active Artboard tool's Scale Artwork with Artboard option for ordinary resizing. Fit to Artwork Bounds and Fit to Selected Art explicitly leave artwork stationary. Dialog regression coverage checks preset/orientation/typed-size intent with scaling on and off, draft cancellation, one-step Undo/Redo, and fitting while Move Artwork and Scale Artwork are enabled. This is a narrow follow-up to #3277; no parity score or estimate is reassessed.

Every known shortfall against Illustrator, one entry each, ranked by how much it stops a professional from switching. This is the work list: unless you were given a task, pick the highest-ranked gap you can make progress on, write a plan, and update the entry (and target-app-parity.md) in the same PR.

Gap ids are stable (PRs say "Part of gap 2"); the rank can change. Hours are Opus 5.5 agent wall-clock hours for one agent, estimated unless marked; calibration in target-app-parity.md. Beta marks the gaps that must close before the beta stage (ROADMAP.md).

Alpha blockers: none. Every core workflow passes the alpha gate; G9 is the only partial one, and it blocks beta, not alpha.

To beta: G1, G9, G10, G11, G12, the corpus and QA part of G8, the type-core part of G4, macOS pen pressure from G14 and the budget run of G15: ~170–270 h one agent, ~50–80 h wall clock with 4–6 agents.

G1 Interaction fidelity

  • Done: Distance Guides (public page): with Smart Guides on and something selected, the Selection tool with Alt/Option held over another object shows the horizontal and vertical distances between them, and over an empty part of an artboard the selection's distances from its four edges, labelled in the General unit; Preferences › Smart Guides › Invoke Distance Guides turns them off. Hover only, as documented: not while moving or nudging. No entry closed; estimates unchanged.

  • Done (part of #4028): Recolor Artwork › Assign: double-clicking a row's new color opens the Color Picker, as the public page describes ("double-click it and select a color in the Color Picker"). OK sets the row's new color in the model it was picked in, so a CMYK mix is no longer a hex value converted back; Cancel leaves the row. A Lab new color is kept, but can't be typed yet: the picker's Lab fields work in RGB, as for fill and stroke. Missing: Lab entry in the picker, swatch libraries in the picker and the row's right-click menu (Pick from Swatches, Limit to Library).

  • Done (#3416): Recolor Artwork Edit chips scroll to the last color while the heading, color wheel and actions stay visible. Screen resize and UI scaling, Preview, Confirm, Cancel, Undo and #1733 wheel drags are covered in tests/recolor.rs. No gap entry closed; estimates unchanged.

  • Polygon/Star count persistence: Exact-size placement saves the chosen count for later drags and reopening the existing canvas dialog. Regression coverage includes both tools, repeated drags, switching tools and Cancel. The remaining G1 scope and estimates are unchanged.

  • Artboard Options shares existing presets and orientation controls and can fit artwork without moving it; artwork fitting includes all drawn document art across artboards and off-board; artwork bounds are cached by active document and revision, and selection uses the shared bounds cache across artboards: Shared existing preset definitions are reused; no external preset assets are added. Presets preserve each selected artboard's orientation, and orientation choices apply even when the active board already matches. Fit operations draft bounds until OK, affect only the active artboard and leave artwork in place. Regression coverage checks draft/Cancel, selected-set application, active-only fitting and Undo. Broader scope and estimates unchanged.

  • Implemented, regression-tested and contributor-confirmed: status messages and readouts use stable responsive allocations sized for localized labels and ordinary coordinates. Original-file acceptance confirmed 2026-10-19; broader G1 scope and estimates unchanged. Sample widths are cached by language, document unit and pixels per point rather than remeasured every frame.

  • Canvas review follow-up: Cached canvas dimensions match the renderer limit before cache-key creation, view construction and worker submission. Controlled-worker regression checks oversized width and height, high DPI and the render transform without allocating oversized images. G1 scope and estimates are unchanged.

  • Done (#3106): while the window is resized, rotated or moved to a screen of another DPI, the cached canvas frame is redrawn at its own scale until the next render, at most the renderer's largest raster size. Broader G1 scope and estimates unchanged.

  • Done: the selection tools take a clipping path (a clip group's or a layer's clipping mask) on its outline, within the selection tolerance, before the art it clips, so Direct Selection reshapes a mask where the art covers its edge; Select Behind lists the same, and the eyedropper and the tools that act on what is drawn are unchanged. Broader G1 estimates unchanged.

  • Done: one selected clip group's Properties panel has Edit Clipping Path and Edit Contents at its top, which select its clipping path or its clipped art for the selection tools (public doc cited in target-app-parity.md). Broader G1 estimates unchanged.

  • Done: the Properties panel has the additional contextual controls of the public Properties panel overview: Blend Options in Quick Actions for one blend with the Blend tool, Merge Live Paint for a Live Paint group selected with more paths to merge (Live Paint Make and Merge refuse type, images and other objects that aren't paths, which used to vanish among the group's sources), the Width Profile list in Appearance with the Width tool or a variable-width stroke, an applied effect's Delete icon beside fx (with several effects it opens the Appearance panel), and Corner and Corner Radius for corners selected with Direct Selection (public doc cited in target-app-parity.md). Broader G1 estimates unchanged.

  • Done (#2691): a selected Grid Repeat (public page) shows a handle below the grid, one right of it and one past its bottom-right corner: dragging them adds or removes rows, columns or both (1 to 500). A slider between the first two columns and one between the first two rows set the horizontal and vertical spacing, staying halfway across the gap under the pointer. Each drag is one undo step through object.repeat.options and Escape cancels it; the controls hide with the edges or the bounding box, and bounding-box handles keep priority where they meet. Radial Repeat handles remain. Estimates unchanged.

  • Done (#2877): a selected Mirror Repeat shows its axis: drag the line or the center handle to move it, an end handle to rotate it (Shift: 45°); each drag is one undo step and Escape cancels it. Bounding-box handles take priority over the axis line; the center and end handles keep their actions. Broader G1 estimates unchanged.

  • Existing-guide Escape cancellation: Selection and Direct/Group Selection clear pending presses and cancel begun guide previews. App-input regressions cover preselected-guide document and interaction-start selection restoration, Undo/Redo and saved state, and later on-canvas motion/release. All eight app-input checks and the Direct Selection Escape control passed in current full CI; Validation evidence. The broader G1 scope and estimate remain unchanged.

  • Done: Artboards menu, trash and Properties delete selected artboards together; selecting all retains artboard 1. Pointer-event regressions cover ordinary artwork, the first-board survivor, Undo/Redo and the single-board guard; broader artboard reports remain open.

  • Done: Artboard Delete/Backspace delete selected boards, retaining the original first when all are selected. The last board and active drags stay protected; headless shortcut regressions cover artwork, saved state and Undo/Redo.

  • Done: status-bar artboard navigation synchronizes the Artboard tool selection before keyboard or Properties deletion, preserving ordinary artwork selection. Actual Next-button regressions cover both deletion keys, Properties Delete, Undo/Redo and other tools in chrome.rs. Tab-switch follow-up: changing the active document through its tab aligns the Artboard tool with the displayed board; same-tab multiselection and Move/Scale Artwork options are preserved. Three tab regressions and historical full CI on a0671777 passed; Validation evidence. The broader G1 scope and estimate remain unchanged. With the Artboard tool active, closing a clean active tab restores the surviving document's displayed board before Properties Delete.

  • Implemented and tested: Undo removes invalid Artboard selection indices without resetting valid multiselection or Move/Scale Artwork options. Headless history tests cover actual panel New/Duplicate, deletion, artwork, object selection, saved state and Undo/Redo; full workspace CI passes.

  • Added: Alt swaps the orientation of a new guide dragged from either ruler. Preview and final placement use the current axis; cancelling preserves the document and Redo, and a completed drag is one undo step. Tool and egui event regressions cover these interactions; the broader G1 pass and estimate remain unchanged.

  • Width-point follow-up: Adjoining adjustments avoid intermediate overflow; non-finite normalized or resulting factors are rejected before committing. Engine regressions cover atomic rejection, Undo/Redo and native save/reopen. Current full CI passed; Validation evidence. The broader G1 pass and estimate remain unchanged.

  • Done: double-click a stroked segment to create a width point through Width Point Edit. Opening, Cancel and deleting the prospective point preserve the document and history; OK creates the point and optionally adjusts adjoining widths in one undo step. Regression and visual evidence: Width-point creation.

  • Done: Shift-double-click opens Width Point Edit with adjoining adjustment enabled. Plain double-click retains the default; dispatch, neighboring widths, Undo/Redo and Cancel have regression coverage.

  • Done (#1227): object clicks with the Artboard tool create a fitted artboard, preserving art and selection; handles, modified clicks and drags retain their meaning. Covered by tool-event regression tests and undo/cancellation checks.

  • Done (#3705, in part): pastes follow the drawing mode (drawing modes): Draw Inside takes Paste, Paste in Place and Paste on All Artboards inside the object drawn into, Draw Behind puts Paste in Place and Paste on All Artboards behind the selection, and Shift+D no longer stops at Draw Behind when one group or other non-path object is selected.

  • Done: Artboard Options' Show Center Mark and Show Cross Hairs (public source): per-artboard checkboxes (artboard.setProps/artboard.new showCenterMark, showCrossHairs) that the canvas draws as a center cross and lines from the middle of each side through the center; exports and print leave them out.

  • Done (#2849): Artboard Options' video display options (public source): Show Video Safe Areas (showVideoSafeAreas) outlines the action-safe area 3.5% and the title-safe area 5% in from each edge, our choice from EBU R 95 (the help page gives no numbers), on the canvas only; Video Ruler Pixel Aspect Ratio (videoRulerPixelAspectRatio, 0.1–10, default 1) is the width of one video pixel over its height. Both per artboard, one undo step, in the native format only when set. View › Rulers › Show Video Rulers is in G7.

  • Done (#3705): Draw Inside in isolation mode (isolation mode): with the object drawn into isolated by a double-click, art drawn or pasted inside it takes isolation mode into its clip group, so it can be clicked and isn't dimmed; it used to stay locked and dimmed beside the isolated path, and double-clicks never reached the clip group.

  • Done: Artboard Options' Show Center Mark and Show Cross Hairs (public source): per-artboard checkboxes (artboard.setProps/artboard.new showCenterMark, showCrossHairs) that the canvas draws as a center cross and lines from the middle of each side through the center; exports and print leave them out. Video safe areas, video rulers and the pixel aspect ratio remain missing.

  • Done: Document Setup → Edit Artboards applies valid settings, closes the dialog and activates the Artboard tool. Pointer-click tests cover successful handoff, invalid settings, OK, Cancel and Undo in dialogs/document_setup.rs.

  • Done (#2691): a double-click on the Line Segment, Arc, Rectangular Grid or Polar Grid tool opens its Tool Options, as the Rectangular Grid tool and Arc tool pages (step 3) and the Tools page describe: the tool's click dialog without a place to draw (Line Segment adds Fill Line; the grids keep their Default Size and Reference Point). OK draws nothing and sets what the next drag draws with and what a click's dialog opens at; Cancel changes nothing. Editing a grid's rows and columns after it is drawn (the rest of #2691) remains. Broader G1 estimate unchanged.

  • Done: Simplify of part of a path, as the manual-simplify page describes for part of a path picked with Direct Selection: with anchors or segments of a path direct-selected, Object › Path › Simplify (the slider, Auto-Simplify and the dialog) refits only each run of selected segments between its end anchors, which stay where they are with their outer handles; the other anchors and segments stay exactly as they were, a closed path's run may cross its start point, separate runs on one path simplify independently in one undo step, and the runs stay selected (object.path.simplify wholePaths: true simplifies such paths whole). Tests: crates/engine/src/tests/simplify_part.rs, simplify_slider_and_dialog_simplify_only_the_direct_selected_part_of_a_path. Broader G1 estimate unchanged.

  • Improved: Curvature uses circular point markers without direction handles or duplicate markers (#1236, in part); real egui frames cover creation, existing paths, Anchor Size and Hide Edges. The request to change interpolation of existing paths remains open.

  • Improved: the Curvature tool's curve: each stretch of three points follows the circle through them (handles along its tangent, chord / (3 cos²(α/2)) long) and the ends of an open path mirror their neighbour's tangent, so a J or a U curves evenly, a turn tighter than 30° comes to a point, and uneven spacing doesn't loop (#1236, in part). The rubber band, dragged, inserted and converted points use the same rule. Re-curving a dragged point's neighbours on an existing path remains open.

  • Improved: Eyedropper has an original pipette cursor at its sampling tip; Use Precise Cursors keeps the crosshair. Bitmap/DPI and preference checks cover the distinction (#1269). OS cursor display and Caps Lock remain unverified.

  • Done (#1251): Eyedropper source reads are independent of locks and isolation, including Shift/Shift+Alt and gradient stops. Source and selection preservation, unchanged Alt reverse/selection restrictions, hidden art and Undo/Redo have regression coverage. This addresses the reported behavior, with no new full-parity measurement.

  • Done (#1253): adding paint to an unpainted zero-width stroke restores the existing 1 pt default, including new-art defaults and Swap Fill/Stroke. The real Eyedropper inheritance sequence, targeted appearance items, preserved widths and Undo/Redo have regression coverage.

  • Done: a busy cursor while a file opens off the UI thread or a labelled background save or export runs (Cursor::Busy in crates/tools/src/cursors.toml). Heavy synchronous effect previews remain open.

  • Missing: Average and Join in one step, with a corner or smooth choice for the joined anchor. path.average and path.join are separate commands and Join has no such choice (coinciding anchors merge into one since #1533). ui-parity.md listed "Join with corner/smooth choice" as done until 2026-10-13. About 1–2 h (estimated), inside the estimate below.

  • Implemented (#1760): Effect › Warp has a shared style selector with original previews, orientation buttons and percent sliders. Existing effects retain their stack slot and target. Focused checks passed and original captures were reviewed; optional Properties integration and remembered defaults remain outside this change.

  • Done (#2120): Smart Guides line extension: dragging the end of a straight segment with Direct Selection or Curvature, the point snaps to the segment's own direction at any angle and the guide runs along it from the other end. Inside the estimate below.

  • Done (#1692): Tab in the Color Picker moves through one color model's fields before the next. Completed upstream before the layout change (#2008).

  • Improved (#2008): Color Picker layout: stacked top-right actions, aligned inputs, less empty space, a distinct header and compact color controls. Narrow windows use stacked sections and vertical scrolling. Pointer/key, warning, layout and mode-switch regressions cover the change; the broader fidelity pass and estimates remain unchanged.

  • Done (#834): bezier drag previews no longer freeze: a Pen, Anchor Point or Direct Selection drag gets every position the pointer is seen at, including the one where it comes back into the window after leaving it and a move in the frame it lets go, so the release commits where the pointer let go; a click's jitter stays a click.

  • Missing (noted for reporters, 2026-10-14): aligning anchor points selected with Direct Selection to a key anchor (from #1636: they align to their bounds; the current public Align page does not say how the key anchor is chosen, so this waits for the owner). Inside the estimate below.

  • Missing: a tool-by-tool, panel-by-panel pass over modifiers, cursors, the Properties panel per context, isolation mode and small behaviours, against the public tool and shortcut documentation. Itemized in ui-parity.md. The Shaper's construction-mode widget and gesture refinements remain.

  • Evidence: no side-by-side session has ever happened (the clean-room rule forbids running Illustrator, so the pass works from the documentation); users keep reporting small differences: #991, #975, #973, #955, #908.

  • Impact: a power user notices this in the first minutes and stops trusting the tool.

  • Estimate: 60–90 h; splits well by tool across agents.

G9 Illustrator .ai and EPS files from real users

  • Done (2026-10-16): EPS legacy mesh corners and vector opacity masks retained; winding-declared compound member groups keep shared paint. Raster print-page minification no longer causes a false editing-data fallback; comparison limits remain unchanged. Synthetic regressions cover damage and missing artwork. This narrows G9; scores and estimates unchanged.

  • Missing: faithful layer and group structure from the editing data in real files (#951: 109 layers instead of 14), guides and non-printing construction lines (#779), open speed on large files (#758), live effects, brushes and symbols as live objects (#637; plain art styles read Drop Shadow, Outer Glow and Feather as live effects; pattern fills and global colours are read since #1025, placed (linked) files since #1264). Writing Illustrator's own editing data is out of scope (undocumented): a PDF-compatible .ai opens in Illustrator 2018 without its layers and groups (#868). Save As .ai › Version: Legacy (version 7) writes the PostScript form from the published version 7 specification instead, keeping layers (names, order, visibility, lock), groups, compound paths, clipping groups, gradients and images, and type as editable text objects (or outlines), one artboard per file (an artboard picker chooses which); transparency, live effects and object names don't survive it (transparent images are flattened or omitted, hidden objects go to a hidden layer, are omitted or made visible), and type is set again in the reader's fonts. Legacy type in .ai files in PostScript form is read on open. It waits for testing by users who hand files back.

  • Evidence: the issues above; 28 of the 350 issues are about .ai/EPS (about 22 people, the most common single format theme), 20 fixed, and the 8 open ones are about structure (layers, guides, speed, live objects), not missing art. No real-file .ai corpus (users' files may be used locally, never committed).

  • Impact: blocks anyone who hands files back to Illustrator users. Opening and reworking their own archive works, with layer cleanup in some files. This is the main-format gap that keeps the stage at alpha.

  • Estimate: 10–20 h with users' files to test against.

G10 Launch and stability on real machines

  • Unconfirmed (2026-10-14): Tool cursors are painted into the window on Wayland (#1652; not run on Linux, #1645 stays open until confirmed). On Windows the custom title bar's window stays truly borderless, so the pointer lines up with what is drawn on systems where the hidden caption offset it (#1791, #1758; awaiting the reporter's confirmation).
  • Done: RPM required dependencies use 64-bit library capabilities and declare glibc 2.35, libm and libgcc_s (#1275); generated metadata and isolated synthetic-provider checks cover x86_64/aarch64. Real-distribution install/start-up QA is still missing.
  • Missing: the app not starting or staying in the background on some Windows 11 machines (#858, #964 fixed 2026-10-10, #620, #818), slow pointer on a Linux AppImage (#575), macOS paste from other apps (#954), a web-free crash/hang reporter, a field record.
  • Evidence: open issues; the never-crash lints and guard stop panics, not driver, windowing or packaging failures.
  • Impact: an app that doesn't start on someone's machine is 0% for them.
  • Estimate: 20–35 h, needs reporters' help on hardware we don't have.

G8 Hardening at scale

  • Done: PngSuite fetching verifies 175 original PNGs and redistribution notices against a pinned SHA-256/size manifest before publishing; file and total-size budgets, cache verification and no archive extraction (#1729). The real-world corpus and manual QA gaps below remain.

  • Done: bounded synthetic control-input expansion (#1709): click/drag counts and pending-event capacity are checked before mutation, and control-channel bursts yield between frames. The corpus and platform QA below remain pending.

  • Done (2026-10-14): WMF/EMF import refuses an oversized embedded PNG or JPEG from its header, before any pixels are decoded (#1776). PDF open no longer takes exponential time on a crafted name tree with shared nodes when it looks for the editing data (#1781). The size limits on a native file's embedded data also apply to files read from memory, not only streamed ones (#1783). Saving over a private file on Unix no longer leaves a readable temporary copy beside it while the file is written (#1778). An Export for Screens suffix can no longer place files outside the export folder (#1777). Package refuses a folder where it would overwrite the open document or one of its linked files (#1786). ruzstd 0.9.1 fixes a decompression bomb (RUSTSEC-2026-0344) reachable from EPS/.ai and Affinity import (#1807). Scatter graph data near the largest number is refused with a message instead of hanging the app (#1780). One very long Liquify stroke segment can no longer create an unbounded number of dabs (#1779). MCP limits: 16 MiB lines, 64-message batches, 256-step command_batch with 8 MiB of kept results and 256 MiB control replies (#1764, fixes #1727). MCP requires the JSON-RPC 2.0 envelope and matches control replies by id, and an app refusal without an id reports the app's reason (#1768, fixes #1728). The corpus and platform QA below remain pending.

  • Done: control sockets have bounded idle, absolute partial-line and reply-write waits (#1726); real TCP tests cover idle, trickled and blocked peers, buffered partial lines, persistent requests and connection-slot recovery. The corpus and platform QA below remain pending.

  • Done (later 2026-10-14): nesting capped at 32 objects across SVG, PDF, EPS and native files, self-using symbols and patterns (#1852); deep or self-referencing PDF and .ai data (#1871), decompression bombs and impossible predictors (#1873, #1700, #1701), self-drawing brushes (#1872), hostile EPS, Affinity and native data (#1863: #1715, #1714, #1704, #1699; save fallback #1695), ids at their largest value, failed command.batch rollback, timed-out control requests and oversized Eyedropper images (#1862: #1718, #1697, #1725, #1717), bounded shadows, glows and stacked Transform effects (#1864: #1706, #1705).

  • Done (2026-10-22): SVG images in SVG images share the reader's depth cap: usvg reads an image while it reads the SVG showing it, on the same stack, so their depths add up, and text/plain and untyped data URLs (which usvg also reads as SVG) are measured as image/svg+xml ones are; an image past the cap is left out with a warning instead of overflowing the stack (#3562). SVGZ images are unpacked before usvg reads them, within one 512 MB cap for all of a file's images, where usvg unpacked a data URL's SVGZ without a cap (#3563).

  • Done (2026-10-22): stacked geometry effects make at most 2 million anchors of a path (of all the paths of a type, symbol or image art together), or the path's own count when that is more. Roughen spaces its points further apart, Zig Zag makes fewer ridges a segment and Free Distort, Twist and the warps split segments into longer pieces where they would pass it, and an effect that would still pass it (Offset Path, Round Corners, a plug-in) is left out. The result is also kept to about 8 million lines for the renderer to draw at 1 px/pt (Wang's formula at vello's 0.25 px tolerance): a large Roughen or Zig Zag draws each point as up to hundreds of lines, so it is built again with fewer points. Three Roughens of a rectangle in a 25 KB file needed tens of gigabytes of geometry, and two million anchors of them 141 million lines (7 GB, past vello's 2²⁷ lines a path); the file now opens in 0.4 s and about 450 MB (#3578). The budget is per path, not per document: many objects that each reach it still add up.

  • Done (2026-10-23): a brushed stroke makes at most 2 million anchors in total, the same figure as the stacked-effects budget above. Pattern tiling and scatter capped each factor on its own (20,000 tiles a run, 4,000 subdivisions a segment, 20,000 copies a track), but those caps are per track and a path has as many tracks as it has subpaths, so they multiplied instead of bounding: one track at its cap measures 20,000 pieces and 320,000 anchors, and sixteen subpaths measured exactly sixteen times that, 5.1 million anchors in 0.57 s. A piece is now taken whole or not at all, and the walk that counts an art tile's anchors charges the whole budget for a tree it cannot finish, so nesting buys no room (#3594). The budget is per brushed stroke, not per document: many strokes that each reach it still add up, and a brush inside a symbol is bounded per stroke rather than per instantiation.

  • Missing: a corpus of real-world SVG/PDF/EPS files; more Affinity versions and platforms (51 pinned files now, including 28 original Affinity 3.2.3 feature probes; large interacting documents and complex typography missing); Windows, Linux and browser QA by hand; packaging polish (Homebrew cask #588, Flathub #554, update checks #615).

  • Impact: unknown failures on users' files.

  • Estimate: 30–50 h (the corpus and QA part blocks beta).

G11 Correctness bugs in core tools

  • Live trace result bounds and selection highlights exclude the retained bitmap except in source-image views: live_trace_result_bounds_exclude_the_retained_bitmap_at_any_angle checks every TraceView, geometric and visual bounds and rotated result bounds. live_trace_selection_highlight_excludes_the_retained_source_rectangle checks result highlights and the existing ordinary-group policy. Shared editing-child traversal also preserves Shaper handling. Broader scope and estimates unchanged.

  • Implemented, Windows native canvas and regression checks passed in PR #2643 (#2544): Anchor Point edits selected blend spine points and handles with path-compatible selection/stacking, handle visibility and 45-degree constraints; #2425 perpendicular segment reshaping is preserved. Broader G11 scope and estimates unchanged.

  • Done (#1968): native saves retain transparency grid visibility without adding an edit or undo step; older files default to hidden. Broader G11 scope and estimates unchanged.

  • Done: Asset Export / raster Art Optimized edges supersample so shapes that meet edge to edge leave no ghost seam (#983, #1037; assets.export abutting-rects regression; Asset Export panel thumbs use the same supersample).

  • Done (2026-10-14): Align and Distribute act on the anchor points selected with Direct Selection: the points of one path align to each other, not to the artboard, and Distribute spaces them (#1641, fixes #1636; aligning to a key anchor is still missing). Delete removes every selected anchor of a closed path (it used to remove the wrong ones), removes objects selected whole along with the selected anchors of others, and keeps the remainder selected so a second Delete removes it (#1674). In isolation mode Direct Selection and Group Selection pick only inside the isolated object (#1666). Escape cancels a Direct Selection drag (#1803, #1743). Escape while typing ends the edit, keeps the type selected and switches to the Selection tool (#1802, #1686, #1656). A filled Pencil path keeps a stroke of None (#1804, part of #1679). In the Pathfinder panel a group selected alone counts its nested shapes, so an expanded stroked object keeps the Shape Modes enabled (#1642, #1635). Object › Expand turns radial, grid and mirror repeats into groups of their instances (#1765, #1756). Select › Same matches type on its characters' fill and stroke (#1746, #1737). Roughen with Smooth keeps turn-backs smooth instead of making cusps that draw as spikes (#1646, #1643). Scribble draws one zig-zag per region, with no lines across holes and notches; convex shapes are unchanged (#1651, #1648).

  • Done: Divide splits filled paths along open cutting lines and curves (#1307), preserving the frontmost filled appearance, implicit filled closure, holes, unrelated objects and one Undo/Redo; the existing bounded-map fallback remains.

  • Done: Numeric fields keep a text drag's start when the pointer gains focus and movement exceeds the click threshold (#1326, in part). A completed focus click selects the whole value; keyboard focus, double-click and numeric stepping remain regression-tested. Short movements still classified as clicks can select all; that case remains open.

  • Done: DXF reads control-point SPLINE closure (#1299 follow-up after #1320); open curves keep their open state. DXF export now recognizes circular cubic paths conservatively and writes native CIRCLE/ARC where stroke semantics permit; R12 weighted strokes remain POLYLINE, and a non-circular ellipse keeps the existing fallback. CNC preset and VCarve QA remain open. Escape leaves Artboard editing for Selection; during a drag it first cancels the gesture. Headless egui key events cover idle Escape, active-drag cancellation and a subsequent Escape in tests/distortkeys.rs.

  • Done: Simplify and Add Anchor Points clear stale component selections on rewritten paths; Simplify previews and reports original/new point counts (#1272).

  • Done: Object › Path › Simplify opens its slider at the Auto-Simplify level for the selection and previews that result, as the manual-simplify page describes; simplifying only a Direct Selection part of a path is done too (G1).

  • Done: no-op anchor Align preserves Undo, Redo, saved state and path geometry (#1180 follow-up), with the same 1e-9 pt tolerance as whole-object Align; actual alignment remains one undo step.

  • Done: Direct Selection picks a segment independently of its anchors and Delete preserves neighboring edges (#1278); scaled text's size and horizontal-scale controls account for object/group transforms (#1034), including exact sizes across grouped labels and resetting horizontal stretch while keeping editable text. Single-result Pathfinder booleans keep source names and SVG IDs, including named groups/compound paths (#1293).

  • Done (later 2026-10-14): the Transform panel's, Properties panel's and Control bar's X/Y/W/H edit the anchor points selected with Direct Selection (#1839, #1824); Snap to Grid wins over Snap to Pixel (#1840, #1816 unconfirmed); Redo during a drag keeps the drag (#1856, #1719); a template layer dims its images by Dim Images instead of fading the whole layer (#1864, #1683); a failed save or export is reported in a dialog that names the file and stays until closed, the document left modified (#1865, #1685).

  • Done: the Shape Builder offers the empty areas closed shapes enclose as regions, such as the middle of four circles that touch, and merges them with the regions around them (#1691).

  • Done (#2523): Shape Builder Gap Detection shares Live Paint's spatially indexed gap finder, including its overshoot/hook safeguards. The existing Shape Builder Tool Options offers Small (3 pt), Medium (6 pt), Large (12 pt) or Custom (up to 72 pt). Temporary bridges are used in detection and merging, but are never added to the art. Off by default; shapeBuilder.merge and shapeBuilder.regions take gap in points. Other existing options are retained. Clicking a stroke in merge mode and broader interaction QA remain.

  • Implemented: deleting an interior anchor of an open path removes its connecting segments and keeps surviving runs separate, without bridging the gap. The remainder stays selected for a second Delete; explicit Remove Anchors still reconnects/refits. Other G11 items and the estimate below remain unchanged.

  • Done (#1910): Transform Each's Reflect X flips left-right and Reflect Y flips top-bottom (aligned with Effect › Distort › Transform). Properties flip buttons keep the reference app's Properties names (Flip Along Horizontal / Vertical Axis).

  • Done (#885): the Transform effect dialog's checkboxes are visible, and it has Transform Objects, Transform Patterns and Scale Strokes & Effects: off, Transform Objects leaves the geometry in place; the other two scale stroke weights, dashes and the fills' and strokes' effect distances and move pattern tiles with the object, copy k by the transformation k times. Canvas, export and Expand Appearance agree. Not yet: a Transform effect in a fill's or stroke's own effect list ignores the two options, and object effects after it keep their distances.

  • Done (#937, reproduced case): Shape Builder regions on art of more than 4,096 segments (traced or type outlines): the planar map no longer gives up there, so lines cut such art instead of the tool offering whole shapes (the planar map's edge-source and face lookups were quadratic in the segments, now indexed, and the cap is 65,536; Divide with open paths shares it). The edge-source index files a long segment under the grid cells along it, so a diagonal hatch (every line's bounds hold most points) no longer costs a scan of the hatch per edge. The grid holds a budget of references (64 per item plus four rows' or columns' worth), the items past it scanned, so coincident segments can't make it quadratic in memory.

  • Done (2026-10-24): Shape Builder line and edge pieces on dense hatches: where the sweep cut a line's way there and its way back a rounding error apart and joined the two cuts with a stub a little over its tolerance, the stub came back as a speck of a piece (lines at exact 0.25 or 0.5 pt steps across a 45° line). The planar map now contracts such stubs into one vertex (within 4× the sweep's tolerance up and down its frame and 1/16 of the 0.01 pt precision along it, bounded by each cluster's extent so a run of tiny level segments keeps its length); regression tests in crates/pathops/src/planar.rs. Estimate unchanged.

  • Missing: SVG units reverting to points (#864); a Transform effect in a fill's or stroke's own effect list ignores Transform Patterns and Scale Strokes & Effects (#885, above). Shape Builder regions (#937, closed), PDF text placement (#722, above), the bezier drag preview (#834, #3065, #3729) and deleting an interior anchor of an open path (above) are done.

  • Done (#722): PDF text opens where the file draws it. Each line used to come in as point type laid out by the font's metrics (its kerning, one even tracking, every glyph on one baseline, a vertical glyph's column an em wide), so glyphs slid wherever the file spaced them otherwise. Now a line takes the font's kerning or none, whichever the file followed, and tracking that puts every glyph where the file drew it (word and character spacing and TJ adjustments per character); text rise (Ts) stays in the line as baseline shift; a vertical glyph is centred on its column by the font's own metrics (/W2, else half its /W or /DW, ISO 32000-1 §9.7.4.3); justified text boxes come back as justified area type. Fixtures written from ISO 32000-1 §9 (tests_text_placement). A font that is neither embedded nor installed still draws in a stand-in with the old fit.

  • Impact: wrong output in everyday work.

  • Estimate: 8–15 h.

A double-click on a port where the frame is threaded breaks the thread there, the story flowing into the frames before the break and the frames after it left empty (text.thread.break; archived help); estimate unchanged.

  • Done (from users' reports): Object › Create Gradient Mesh on an embedded image turns it into a mesh over its rectangle, with the image's transform kept; each point takes the average colour and opacity of the picture around it (#1676). A linked image is refused, as the public documentation has it.

  • Partial: blend easing (#1124, 30.7): Window › Blend has Type (Ease In, Ease Out, Ease In Out, Ease Out In), Ramp 0–100% and independent color Shift; easing is disabled without a spine. The original polynomial distributions approximate the public description. On-canvas easing handles and their synchronization remain missing. Public source.

  • Done: gradient Dither (30.0): the Gradient panel's Dither box (paint.editGradient dither, also in paint.setFill's gradient, swatches and the native file) draws a linear or radial gradient fill as pixels with seeded noise of up to a colour level, which hides banding on the canvas and in raster exports; SVG and PDF exports write the fill as an image at the Document Raster Effects resolution, and PDF with Preserve Editing keeps the gradient editable. Fills only, as the public documentation says. Freeform gradients ignore it.

  • Done: gradient Method (30.0): the Gradient panel's Method menu, Classic or Perceptual (paint.editGradient method, also in paint.setFill's gradient, swatches and the native file, written only when Perceptual). Perceptual mixes a linear or radial gradient's colours in OKLab, so blue to yellow passes through a light blue-grey rather than mid grey; renderers draw it through stops on that curve (within half a colour level), and SVG and PDF exports write it as an image at the Document Raster Effects resolution, as the public documentation says perceptual gradients are rasterised there. Classic draws exactly as before; freeform gradients mix their own way. With Dither, a Perceptual fill is the perceptual mix with dither's noise (an image with the noise in SVG and PDF); a stroke has no noise.

  • Missing (asked for by users, from earlier versions): radial gradients in Image Trace's Gradients option, which traces linear ones only (draft #1849). Inside the estimate below.

  • Partial (#2530): tangent snapping to curves and perpendicular snapping to straight target segments for drawn lines. Controls are saved under Preferences › Smart Guides › Geometric Guides and available from Control bar › Snapping; both default to on. Existing-line endpoint editing and other tool cases remain unverified. Public source.

  • Missing: gradient presets (30.0); remaining tangent/perpendicular snapping cases and the consolidated snapping options (30.0); artboard colors in exports and print, and managing artboards from the canvas other than locking and unlocking them from the Artboard tool's right-click menu (30.0); the Blend panel with ease in/out and separate colour acceleration (30.7); the Dimension tool (28.x).

  • Evidence: Adobe's 30.0 and 30.7 release announcements, see target-app-parity.md.

  • Estimate: 13–23 h.

G5 Brushes, symbols and libraries

  • Done: Symbol Options › Registration (9-point; stored and used by symbol.place); Symbol Options › Export Type (Graphic or Movie Clip; default Movie Clip; symbol.new / symbol.options / Symbols panel; canvas placement unchanged; Animate / Flash handoff metadata); Symbol Options › Enable Guides for 9-Slice Scaling (four guides as fractions of the symbol size, nineSlice / nineSliceGuides on symbol.new / symbol.options, stored per symbol; handoff metadata, not drawn on the canvas, #2342); Brush Options › Key Color eyedropper for scatter, art and pattern brushes (Hue Shift colorization; samples canvas art); Select › Start Global Edit (#3521) on paths, compound paths and symbol instances: the objects of the same shape at any place and size, narrowed by Appearance, Size and the artboards to search, take an edit of any one of them in proportion, as one undo step (public source). Color eyedropper for scatter, art and pattern brushes (Hue Shift colorization; samples canvas art); symbol libraries (public source): Window › Symbol Libraries and the Symbols panel's Symbol Libraries Menu open each library in a library panel of its own (one original library generated in code, Basic Shapes; User Defined; Other Library… reads the symbols of any document VectorCraft opens); a click adds a symbol to the document's Symbols with its Symbol Options and the resources it uses, as one undo step, and dragging one onto the canvas also places it; Save Symbols / Save Symbol Library writes the document's symbols as a .vectorcraft library into the user library folder (listed under User Defined) or a file (symbol.libraries, symbol.addFromLibrary, symbol.saveLibrary, symbol.loadLibrary); brush libraries (public source, import): Window › Brush Libraries and the Brushes panel's Brush Libraries Menu open each library in a library panel of its own (four original libraries generated in code: Art Ribbons, Calligraphic Nibs, Pattern Borders, Scatter Shapes; User Defined; Other Library… reads the brushes of any document VectorCraft opens); a click adds a brush to the document's Brushes with the patterns, symbols and other resources its art uses, as one undo step (applied to the selected paths in the same step), dragging one onto a path adds and applies it and dragging one onto the Brushes panel adds it; Save Brushes / Save Brush Library writes the document's brushes as a .vectorcraft library into the user library folder (listed under User Defined) or a file (brush.libraries, brush.addFromLibrary, brush.saveLibrary, brush.loadLibrary).
  • Missing: the Art brush's Overlap, auto-generated Pattern brush corners, new tile art in Pattern Brush Options; more built-in brush, symbol and graphic-style libraries (original, generated in code, never Adobe's); dynamic symbols; Global Edit of similar groups (edits to an object inside a group reaching the matching objects of similar groups, public source), rotated copies as matches, Shift-click to leave a match out and highlighting matches before the start; drawing the 9-slice guides on the canvas in symbol edit mode and scaling by them. Options; more built-in brush and symbol libraries (original, never Adobe's); dynamic symbols; Start Global Edit; drawing the 9-slice guides on the canvas in symbol edit mode and scaling by them.

G3 3D and Materials

  • Done: an initial live Revolve in the three-d crate (#846, from the contributor who offered in #605), with automatic smooth vector shading, default-on circular caps and spike-free continuous rims; Extrude & Bevel, Inflate and Rotate with Position presets (three-d.md, #1407). Colored Inflate has automatic smooth vector lighting from shared membrane normals. White-light Inflate keeps its existing appearance. All four take one to ten colored directional lights, with neutral ambient applied once, a light list and independent previewing controls. Standard, Diffuse, Top Left and Right select original rigs, shared with commands; manual settings show Custom.

  • Impact: specialist; Materials is the one menu stub left.
  • Estimate: 25–45 h; plan in plan/ before coding.

G7 Views and windows

Estimate unchanged.

Shift-snapping a new guide to ruler ticks still uses the General unit's ticks. Estimate unchanged.

Edit Views… lists them to rename or delete, applied together on OK as one undo step (view.saved.edit {edits}); a file's views are checked when it opens. Estimate unchanged.

G6 Automation and scripting

  • Missing: a scripting surface over the command registry (Illustrator: JavaScript, File › Scripts; #1183 is open). Actions, Batch, Variables (text, visibility, image and graph), data set CSV import and export, and full agent control over MCP are done.
  • Estimate: 4–8 h.
  • Done (2026-10-16): the MCP server hears the client during a long call: notifications/cancelled stops a queued or running export (PDF pages, flattening, baking, drawing, artboards) without writing anything or changing the document, ping and the list methods answer at once, any other request that would wait behind a call running for two seconds or more is refused as busy (-32003, naming the call), and _meta.progressToken gets page progress (#2165, #2171, #2172). Reading the document during an export is not served (refused as busy); estimate unchanged.
  • Exposed in MCP: add_text {vertical: true} uses the existing vertical point, area and path type commands. Horizontal writing remains the default; the broader automation gap and estimate are unchanged.

G15 Performance budgets and a GPU renderer

  • Improved (#1257): Craquelure, Mosaic Tiles and Stained Glass reuse squared distances during nearest-cell searches, with the original distance ordering retained near rounding/tie boundaries. A brute-force boundary regression and full-viewport pixel comparisons agree with the old result. texture_drag_perf reproduces a moved CMYK rounded rectangle at 190.07% and DPI 1.5; timings from a busy development machine are supporting evidence, with idle Windows drag QA still pending.
  • Missing: an idle-machine run of vectorcraft-cli perf at 50k paths (2026-10-11 at 25k paths, every budget met, 400% zoom 12.3 ms against 16 ms, measured; runs of 0.10.0 on Linux with 4 logical CPUs, reported in #1172 on 2026-10-13, missed all three render budgets at 20k paths), a spatial index for zoomed-in frames, dirty-region rendering, the GPU backend spike (M5). Large-selection edits, cached live effects and Pathfinder Trim, Merge, Crop and Outline landed in #1173.
  • Estimate: 15–25 h (the budget run and fixes block beta).

G16 Localization: the three missing key languages

  • Evidence: Brazilian Portuguese catalog complete under the tests (menus, literals, messages; one|other plurals; #1914). Vietnamese catalog complete under the tests (menus, literals, messages; one plural form). Czech render-site bypasses reduced in file dialogs, diagnostics, preset names and contributor tooltips; gradient grammar and printer-mark context corrected (see localization-parity.md). Native review and the remaining missing-language work remain.

  • Missing: Hindi, Arabic, Indonesian catalogs; a Korean UI font for the web build; a right-to-left interface and interface shaping for Arabic and Devanagari; messages for Simplified Chinese; native review of every catalog. Measured in localization-parity.md.

  • Estimate: 50–85 h plus human review (Brazilian Portuguese completed 2026-10-14).

G17 Ecosystem: third-party plug-ins

  • Missing: Illustrator's ecosystem is a C++ plug-in SDK and a large commercial plug-in market. VectorCraft has sandboxed WebAssembly plug-ins for object filters, live effects and file formats it writes (plugins.md) and MCP; missing are tool plug-ins, panel plug-ins, importers, a plug-in directory and any third-party plug-ins (#710).
  • Done: exporter plug-ins ("kind": "exporter"). A plug-in adds a write-only file format that File › Export › Export As lists after the built-in ones and document.export writes (plugin.<id>, or a path ending in one of its extensions). It is given the document as the native file's JSON and its parameters, with a larger budget than a filter's, which Background Export's Cancel stops; the host writes the file it returns, and nothing when it declines or returns bad data. Engine, ABI and headless Export As regressions.
  • Done: a plug-in's parameters say how its dialogs show them: label, unit, help, helpUrl, group (sections that fold) and visibleWhen (shown only while the checkboxes and choices it names have one of the listed values). string and numberList parameters join the others, and a plug-in declares up to 256, at most 64 outside groups. The filter, live-effect and exporter dialogs use them, and the Appearance panel's effect editor the labels, units, help and conditions; hosts from before the keys ignore them. Manifest unit tests and kittest dialog regressions.
  • Done: a live effect is given its object's fills and strokes, read only, as a filter is, and _context.item says which fill or stroke it sits on; a change of paint runs it again. Engine and unit regressions.
  • Done: a filter is given its objects' effect records and their strokes' join, cap and miter limit, and may return both: the records are admitted as effect.apply admits them (one refused refuses the output), so a tool can set up objects for a live effect in one step. A path a filter hands back unchanged stays a live shape. Engine and unit regressions.
  • Done: a filter keeps data with the document (documentData, at most 1 MiB, in the same undo step as its objects) and reads it back in _context.documentData. It is the document's foreign data (unknown.pluginData), so the native file keeps it with no section of its own, and an exporter finds it in the document it is given. Engine and unit regressions.
  • Done: a filter may ask for a heavy budget ("budget": "heavy": 1 G instructions and 300 s a run), for routing, packing or simulation. Installing it asks the user first (allowHeavy; folders skip it), and the app runs it on a thread of its own with a progress window and Cancel, applying its result as one undo step unless the document changed meanwhile. ABI, engine and headless UI regressions.
  • Estimate: 20–45 h for the APIs; the ecosystem itself isn't agent work.

G18 Generative AI features

  • Missing: Text to Vector Graphic, Generative Recolor, Generative Shape Fill (#766), Generative Expand, Concept to Vector, Prompt to Edit, Rewrite Text. Adobe's run on its cloud models; ours would be a pluggable provider.
  • Needs: an owner decision on models and providers.
  • Estimate: 30–60 h after that decision.

G19 Accessibility

  • Missing: AccessKit is on by default, so egui widgets reach screen readers, but custom panels, the canvas and its objects aren't described and nothing has been tested with VoiceOver, Narrator or Orca; keyboard-only canvas operation; high contrast. Illustrator's own accessibility is limited, so this is mostly beyond parity.
  • Done: PDF export writes /ViewerPreferences << /DisplayDocTitle true >> when File Info has a Document Title (or an explicit export title is supplied), so viewers and accessibility checkers use that title instead of the file name (#3646).
  • Estimate: 15–25 h.

Highlighted-text Eyedropper (2026-10-21)

Type/Eyedropper switches preserve highlighted characters; sampling changes only their enabled font/paint attributes. Enabled non-neutral source or target object transparency is refused atomically; disable Transparency to preserve object transparency while sampling the range. tests/eyedropper.rs covers ranges, Unicode, history and transparency; tool tests cover brush-key sampling coexistence. Scores and estimates unchanged. See development.md.

Drag artwork between document tabs (2026-10-22)

Selection drags activate another visible document tab after 400 ms, then copy editable artwork on canvas release with the original grab point. Source and clipboard preservation, resource rendering, swatch conflicts, cancellation, rotated/zoomed views and target Undo/Redo have regression coverage (tests_document_drag, tests_clipboard). Overflow-menu and cross-window drag remain separate. Scores and hours unchanged. Behavior and command details.

Pathfinder › Trap (2026-10-23)

The Pathfinder panel menu's Trap… (object.pathfinder.trap) and Effect › Pathfinder › Trap… (pathfinder.trap) ship, from the public trapping and Pathfinder panel pages: where two objects' visible areas of different solid colours meet, an overprinting strip of the lighter colour goes into the darker one (Reverse Traps: the other way, but not a rich black), with Thickness, Height/Width, Tint Reduction and Traps with Process Color, and in the effect Precision and Remove Redundant Points. The panel's Trap is one undo step and groups the traps above the topmost selected object. Effect › Pathfinder is complete (13/13); the Live vector effects missing list no longer names Hard Mix, Soft Mix or Trap. Left: gradient and pattern fills don't trap, and the defaults (0.25 pt, 100%, 40%) are VectorCraft's own, the pages give none. Tests: crates/engine/src/tests/trap.rs, crates/effects/src/trap.rs, crates/pathops/src/trap.rs.

2026-10-14minorNo entry closed. G11: Align and Distribute act on the anchor points selected with Direct Selection: the points of one path align to each other, not to the artboard, and Distribute spaces them (#1641, fixes #1636; aligning to a key anchor is still missing); Delete removes every selected anchor of a closed path (it used to remove the wrong ones), removes objects selected whole along with the selected anchors of others, and keeps the remainder selected so a second Delete removes it (#1674); In isolation mode Direct Selection and Group Selection pick only inside the isolated object (#1666); Escape cancels a Direct Selection drag (#1803, #1743); Escape while typing ends the edit, keeps the type selected and switches to the Selection tool (#1802, #1686, #1656); A filled Pencil path keeps a stroke of None (#1804, part of #1679); In the Pathfinder panel a group selected alone counts its nested shapes, so an expanded stroked object keeps the Shape Modes enabled (#1642, #1635); Object › Expand turns radial, grid and mirror repeats into groups of their instances (#1765, #1756); Select › Same matches type on its characters' fill and stroke (#1746, #1737); Roughen with Smooth keeps turn-backs smooth instead of making cusps that draw as spikes (#1646, #1643); Scribble draws one zig-zag per region, with no lines across holes and notches; convex shapes are unchanged (#1651, #1648). G8: WMF/EMF import refuses an oversized embedded PNG or JPEG from its header, before any pixels are decoded (#1776); PDF open no longer takes exponential time on a crafted name tree with shared nodes when it looks for the editing data (#1781); The size limits on a native file's embedded data also apply to files read from memory, not only streamed ones (#1783); Saving over a private file on Unix no longer leaves a readable temporary copy beside it while the file is written (#1778); An Export for Screens suffix can no longer place files outside the export folder (#1777); Package refuses a folder where it would overwrite the open document or one of its linked files (#1786); ruzstd 0.9.1 fixes a decompression bomb (RUSTSEC-2026-0344) reachable from EPS/.ai and Affinity import (#1807); Scatter graph data near the largest number is refused with a message instead of hanging the app (#1780); One very long Liquify stroke segment can no longer create an unbounded number of dabs (#1779); MCP limits: 16 MiB lines, 64-message batches, 256-step command_batch with 8 MiB of kept results and 256 MiB control replies (#1764, fixes #1727); MCP requires the JSON-RPC 2.0 envelope and matches control replies by id, and an app refusal without an id reports the app's reason (#1768, fixes #1728). G10, unconfirmed: Tool cursors are painted into the window on Wayland (#1652; not run on Linux, #1645 stays open until confirmed); On Windows the custom title bar's window stays truly borderless, so the pointer lines up with what is drawn on systems where the hidden caption offset it (#1791, #1758; awaiting the reporter's confirmation). A clause repeated in two G11 bullets is there once. Estimates unchanged
2026-10-13minorNo entry closed. Pathfinder's Trim, Merge and Crop remove the objects' strokes, and Merge joins same-fill objects whatever their strokes were, as the public Pathfinder page describes (#1572, fixes #1570); Warp › Arc (the effect and Envelope › Make with Warp) bends in the object's real proportions: a circular arc with concentric edges and no fold-over at 100%, so Arc on art that isn't square draws differently from before (#1581, fixes #1578); Offset Path with an inset larger than the shapes says the offset leaves nothing, instead of asking to select paths (#1591, fixes #1590); A zero-length subpath draws its round cap as a dot and its projecting cap as a square, so dots in imported .ai and SVG files show (#1619, fixes #1613); Area type in a non-rectangular shape moves a word too wide for the top lines down to the first line that holds it instead of breaking it (#1617, fixes #1615); Tool flyouts are as wide as their longest translated name and shortcut need, so names no longer run into shortcuts in Spanish and other languages (#1650, fixes #1616); Saving to a network drive on macOS falls back to a plain fsync when the share refuses a full flush (#1625, part of #1620; not confirmed on a real share), and a save still succeeds when a folder refuses the temporary file, the rename over the document or copying permissions: the content is written elsewhere first and copied in, and a failed copy keeps the temporary file and names it (#1649, part of #1620); Smart Guides: a point drawn with the Pen or a shape tool, and an anchor dragged with Direct Selection, snaps to where paths and ruler guides cross, labelled "intersect" (#1658, part of #1602; a moved selection's own anchors don't); estimates unchanged

G11: Make Compound Path on a group (such as outlined type) keeps the paint of its backmost path instead of drawing nothing, and compound paths joined into one keep their holes (#1537); a round corner next to a curved side curves smoothly instead of sticking out of the shape and the Smooth tool smooths only the stretch of path under the drag (#1547, fixes #1512); Raster effects (blur, shadow, glow, grain) drawn after a pattern, radial or freeform gradient fill export at their place and size (#1541, fixes #1536). G9: a multi-artboard .ai with notes beside its artboards opens from its editing data, a page's art past its artboard no longer lying over the page before it (#1528); a .ai gradient whose stops are listed upwards keeps each midpoint on the stop that starts its part of the ramp (#1530); SVG text on a path follows basic shapes (circle, ellipse, rect, line, polyline, polygon) as their SVG 2 equivalent paths (#1531, fixes #1527); PDFs whose alpha soft masks are drawn as images import with the mask instead of empty art (#1551); EPS and PostScript type set in Type 42 (TrueType) fonts imports at its size instead of 1000 times too large (#1553); PDF and EPS import keep a clipping path whose bounding box covers the page but whose shape doesn't (#1544, fixes #1542); Paste takes a PDF or EPS another app copied as editable vector art: from the macOS pasteboard (with SVG), EPS on Windows beside PDF, and .eps files copied in a file manager, with the new command clipboard.importEps (#1538, fixes #1499); Opening or placing a file with an image too large to decode says so, and the Links panel shows it on the row (#1540, part of #1479). Native documents with a lot of path data (traced or generated art, in layers, symbols or patterns) are saved as compact JSON, about a fifth of the size; small documents stay pretty-printed (#1492); the font scan on Linux also reads the folders fontconfig's configuration lists, such as TeX fonts under /usr/share/texmf/fonts (#1548, fixes #1529; not verified on Linux); Polish catalog (#1498); estimates unchanged, no gap entry closed
